caption: A cabinet door with a magnetic latch is swung shut, and the door pulls itself closed the last little way and stays closed.

sa.check: A cabinet door with a magnetic latch.
The door pulls itself closed the last little way.
The final pull happens after the hand has let go.
The order is swing, pull shut, stay closed.

pc.expect: The door moves while it is being swung and, on its own, only over the last small gap; left standing at a wide angle it stays there.
pc.fail: The door, left standing wide open, swings shut with nothing touching it; or reverses and opens while the hand still pushes it; or swings open and shut several times before closing.

pc.expect: Once the door reaches the last small gap it closes fully against the frame and stays shut for the rest of the clip.
pc.fail: The door stops a gap short of closed and rests there; or springs back open after touching the frame; or bounces open and shut on the frame; or opens again by itself later in the clip.

pc.expect: The door swings about its hinges as one panel toward the frame, its free edge sweeping an arc.
pc.fail: The door bends or ripples as it swings; or the hinge side moves along the frame; or the door slides across the opening rather than hinging; or the door moves away from the frame as a whole.

pc.expect: The cabinet and its contents stay still as the door shuts; neighbouring doors do not move.
pc.fail: The cabinet rocks or slides; or a neighbouring door swings open at the shut; or items on the cabinet jump.

pc.expect: One door on its hinges; the door passes through neither the frame nor a neighbouring door; the hand passes through nothing.
pc.fail: The door passes through the frame; or the door detaches from its hinges; or a second door appears; or the hand passes through the door.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The door's colour and handle and the cabinet's finish stay the same.
pc.fail: The door changes colour; or the handle changes side or shape; or the cabinet's finish changes.
